clue.text: Tethers donkey to dispose of the weed incessantly

parts.note: tethers are the chains or ropes that tie up an animal
moke is British slang for a donkey

explanation.surface: Someone ties up a donkey before getting rid of some troublesome weeds without pause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The weed' is a slang name for tobacco, not a garden plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Smoking cigarettes one after another, lighting each from the last, consumes tobacco without a break.

clue.text: Tool that has retractable claws

definitions.meaning: a dupe exploited by someone else to do their dirty work
read literally, the foot of a feline, whose claws draw back in

explanation.definitionFit: A person used as a pawn by another is a tool; a feline's foot literally sheathes its claws.

clue.text: Weapon carried by powerful jazzman

indicators.note: in a down clue the weapon sits on top of the next word, as if carried by it

parts.note: an arm is a weapon, as in firearms
powerful means strong

explanation.surface: A mighty jazz musician is pictured carrying a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: Louis Armstrong was the celebrated New Orleans trumpeter and singer, a jazz musician.

clue.text: Keep one's upper lip stiff when speaking Latin

definitions.text: Keep one's upper lip stiff when speaking Latin

parts.words: Keep one's upper lip stiff when speaking Latin
parts.note: a Latin motto meaning never give up hope, the classical way of telling someone to stay stoical

explanation.definitionFit: The Latin tag, from Horace, urges perseverance without despair, the stoic resolve of a stiff upper lip.

clue.text: Young lady and I have entered into correspondence

parts.note: a miss is a young unmarried woman
contracted to I've, with the apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: A girl and the speaker have started writing letters to each other.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Entered into' is only a link here, not a container signal: the pieces simply sit side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal letter is an item of written correspondence.

clue.text: Brown family party

parts.note: recalls the old cockney music-hall singalong in which Mother Brown is urged to dance at a lively celebration

explanation.walkthrough: The clue alludes to the London music-hall song about Mother Brown dancing, sung at boisterous British parties.
explanation.definitionFit: A lively, noisy party with dancing is a British informal term taken from that song.

clue.text: With second whip, beat it!

parts.note: cat as in cat-o'-nine-tails, a many-tailed whip

explanation.surface: A command to flee given to someone holding a second whip.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are brusque commands telling someone to go away at once.

clue.text: Feature duck and another sturdy fabric

parts.note: the chin is one of the facial features
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, so the letter O

explanation.surface: A facial feature, a waterbird and a heavy cloth are listed together.
explanation.walkthrough: Duck is itself a strong cotton cloth, which is why the definition says 'another' sturdy fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: A hard-wearing twilled cotton cloth used for trousers, like duck a tough textile.

clue.text: Chesterton's man coming before Defoe's

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'Chesterton's man coming before Defoe's', points to THURSDAY (Chesterton's The Man Who Was Thursday, before Defoe's Man Friday), which does not fit the 7-letter answer TUESDAY; clue and answer appear mismatched.

clue.text: Not so ecstatic when the policeman appeared?

definitions.text: Not so ecstatic when the policeman appeared?

parts.words: Not so ecstatic when the policeman appeared?
parts.note: the seaside puppet villain gleefully clubs the constable puppet whenever he arrives, so the phrase for delight is read literally

explanation.walkthrough: In a traditional British Punch and Judy puppet show, Mr Punch beats the policeman with his stick.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means very happy and satisfied, delighted short of rapture.

clue.text: Oriental language Frenchman used in the end

indicators.note: used in places the Frenchman's letter inside the word for the end

parts.note: the tail is the end of something
M is the abbreviation for Monsieur, a Frenchman

explanation.surface: A Frenchman eventually resorts to an Eastern tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: A Dravidian tongue spoken in southern India and Sri Lanka, Asian and so oriental.

clue.text: Soldiers at the front taking severe punishment from this?

definitions.text: Soldiers at the front taking severe punishment from this?

parts.words: Soldiers at the front taking severe punishment from this?
parts.note: troops in the front line suffer bombardment from enemy artillery

explanation.definitionFit: Explosive projectiles fired by guns are what punish front-line troops.

clue.text: Staffs area supplying services

definitions.meaning: the ceramics district of north Staffordshire around Stoke-on-Trent
factories that make tea and dinner sets of crockery

explanation.walkthrough: Staffs is the short form of Staffordshire, an English county; 'services' are sets of matching china, not help.
explanation.definitionFit: The ceramic-making towns of Stoke are known by that name, and such works produce china sets.

clue.text: Duck to provide an opportunity for ruffing?

definitions.meaning: to duck is to dodge or evade

definitions.text: to provide an opportunity for ruffing?
definitions.meaning: in bridge, holding no cards of a suit lets a player trump, or ruff, when it is led

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the word into an article and a bridge term for an empty suit.
explanation.definitionFit: To dodge something is to steer clear of it; an empty suit in bridge allows trumping.

clue.text: Sort of cushion made for celebration

definitions.meaning: a rubber joke cushion that makes a rude noise when sat on
boisterous merrymaking, as in the phrase with make

explanation.walkthrough: 'Made for' nods to the idiom of making merry in this way.
explanation.definitionFit: A prank inflatable cushion bears this name, and it also means noisy revelry.

clue.text: Be nosy about one and all, telling people how to behave

indicators.note: about means the nosy word goes round the other piece

parts.note: to pry is to be nosy
each means one and all, every individual

explanation.surface: A busybody snoops on everyone while lecturing them on manners.
explanation.definitionFit: Moralising and sanctimonious, inclined to lecture others on conduct.

clue.text: Partner and I joining a lot of business associations

parts.note: a consort is a partner, especially a spouse

explanation.surface: Someone and their partner join several trade bodies.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin-style plural names several groups of companies formed for a joint venture.

clue.text: Take unfair share of paintings, hard for artist

parts.note: to hog is to take more than one's fair share
art means paintings collectively
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Grabbing too many paintings is tough on the painter.
explanation.definitionFit: William Hogarth was the eighteenth-century English painter and engraver.

clue.text: Son's in a stew, in a dangerous situation

indicators.note: in tells us the son goes inside the stew

parts.note: a hotpot is a Lancashire stew of meat topped with sliced potato
S is the abbreviation for son, with 's meaning is

explanation.surface: A son is worried and in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a stew' looks like the idiom for agitated; here the stew is a Lancashire hotpot, a British dish.
explanation.definitionFit: A place of conflict or danger, a flashpoint, is described by this phrase.

clue.text: Produce cuttings showing journalist understood

parts.note: a hack is a journalist, often a disparaging term
saw means understood, as in I saw what you meant

explanation.surface: A reporter grasped how press cuttings are made.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cuttings' suggests newspaper clippings to go with the journalist; here they are cuts made by a saw.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as a verb, it means to cut through metal with a fine-toothed frame saw.

clue.text: Native American author born here

parts.note: George Bernard Shaw, the Irish playwright and author
née, French for born, introduces a maiden name

explanation.surface: A writer of Native American descent was born in this place.
explanation.definitionFit: An Algonquian-speaking people of North America, originally of the Ohio valley.

clue.text: Extravagantly spend money to put in shrub

indicators.note: put in means the money is placed inside the plant's name

parts.note: spurge is a euphorbia, a plant genus including shrubby species
L stands for pound, from the Latin libra, British money

explanation.surface: Lavish spending on cash to bury in a bush.
explanation.definitionFit: To spend freely and lavishly on a treat is to go on a binge of spending.

clue.text: sounded exhausted, as far as one can see

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'sounded exhausted, as far as one can see', begins in lower case and seems cut short: the wordplay needs a word sounding like EYE (presumably 'I') before 'sounded'.
annotationWithheld.clue: sounded exhausted, as far as one can see

clue.text: Humorous writer's novel I want

indicators.note: novel means new or reworked, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone longs for a comic author's novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like a book to go with the writer, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Mark Twain, the American author of Tom Sawyer, was celebrated for comic writing.

clue.text: For each person in front

definitions.meaning: split in two, the phrase means per individual, as in a cost charged at so much apiece

explanation.definitionFit: Charging so much per capita is per individual; being in the lead is being forward of others.

clue.text: Room quiet? Hard with individual on this

definitions.text: Room quiet? Hard with individual on this

parts.note: a cell is a small room, as in a prison or monastery
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, quiet
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard
one means a single individual

explanation.surface: It is hard to keep a room quiet with someone talking on a mobile.
explanation.definitionFit: A portable telephone, a mobile, is the device someone is talking on.

clue.text: Person in the past, before modern computer device?

parts.note: pre- is a prefix meaning before
a cursor is the on-screen pointer of a computer

explanation.surface: Someone from history is set against modern computing.
explanation.definitionFit: A forerunner or predecessor is someone who came earlier.

clue.text: Cut both taps after negative start

indicators.note: after means the taps follow the negative piece

parts.note: not is a negative
C and H mark the cold and hot taps

explanation.surface: Someone cuts off the water at both taps once things begin badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Start' only confirms that the negative comes first; taps are labelled C (cold) and H (hot).
explanation.definitionFit: A V-shaped cut or nick in an edge.

clue.text: Commotion requiring action

definitions.meaning: still waiting to be done, as items on a list of tasks

explanation.definitionFit: A fuss or rumpus is one sense; tasks pending are another.

clue.text: Bridge player requiring very little the skill of adoring partner

parts.note: S for South, one of the four players at bridge
wee is Scottish for small, very little
art means skill

explanation.surface: A card player needs scant skill to be a devoted partner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Partner' points to bridge; here it is a loved one.
explanation.definitionFit: A loved one or darling, a romantic partner who dotes.
